currentContext.expansion: Mindteck is an asset-light IT and engineering services business and the routed sections disclose no plant, capacity addition or rupee capital-expenditure plan. Expansion is described purely as capability build-out: a dedicated AI Centre of Excellence (CoE) that drives innovation across product engineering, data engineering and quality engineering services and underpins reusable AI frameworks, accelerators and industry-specific solutions; a growing focus on Digital Engineering layered onto the core Embedded Systems, Enterprise Applications and Quality Assurance portfolio; and continued alignment of the organisation structure across Mindteck with business goals. Delivery footprint is described only as a best-shore model blending onsite, offshore, near-shore and hybrid approaches. Growth in FY26 came through named client engagements rather than physical build-out - a strategic FPGA conversion engagement in Test and Measurement, next-gen digital axle counter solutions for railway safety, Android BSP development, a lighting-control interface programme with further products in development (WaveX, Z-Wave dimmer, warm dim, CMS6990-based current controllers V1 and V2, linear starter, Flutter-based commissioning UI, RGBW systems), and a cloud migration to Microsoft Azure for a UK-based renewable energy provider now sustained through ongoing managed operations. No commissioning dates, site counts, headcount capacity or delivery-centre additions are stated in this bundle.

risks are slower IT budgets, vendor competition and keeping pace with AI-ready and software-defined storage.|Analytical instruments: outlook described as positive with mid- to high-single-digit CAGR, driven by pharma/biotech R&D, environmental and regulatory testing, semiconductor process control, and automation/AI-enabled analytics; constrained by high capital cost and long replacement cycles.|Medical devices: steady mid-single-digit growth supported by aging populations, chronic disease burden, minimally invasive and AI-enabled devices, wearables and home monitoring; pressured by value-based contracting, regulatory complexity and reimbursement.|Semiconductor: outlook described as strongly positive, with AI demand, data-centre buildout and memory growth driving a record market; risks from tariffs, trade policy, energy access and supply-chain volatility.|Energy and utilities: sharp load growth from AI data centres and electrification driving investment in capacity, grid modernisation, analytics and resilience; opportunities in grid modernisation, renewable integration, storage and energy analytics.|Outsourcing market backdrop: BPO projected to grow over 9% annually through 2030 and the total outsourcing market to reach around USD 800 billion by 2033, with nearshore and hybrid models, outcome-based engagements, AI-augmented services and higher-value talent as the stated 2026 trends.|Software/services backdrop: agentic AI shifting the industry to AI-first engineering, intensifying competition between AI-natives and incumbents, and rising cybersecurity complexity - cited as the operating environment for 2026.|No order book or pipeline figure is disclosed. The Board's Report instead lists named FY26 engagement wins, including a strategic engagement for advanced FPGA conversion services in Test and Measurement, a next-gen digital axle counter programme for railway safety, Android BSP development, a firmware and language verification testing partnership with a UK-based client, obsolescence management for a portfolio of products of a leading US-based company, and a cloud migration to Microsoft Azure for a leading UK-based renewable energy provider managing real-time data from 80,000 smart meters, now sustained through ongoing managed operations.
